utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everybody this afternoon. Mr. Registrar, will you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you. Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is Case number IT-04-83-T, Prosecutor versus Rasim Delic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. May we have the appearances for today.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good afternoon, Your Honours, Counsel, and everyone in and around the courtroom. For the Prosecution, Daryl Mundis and Matthais Neuner, assisted by our case manager, Alma Imamovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. I'm Vasvija Vidovic, Nicholas David Robson representing General Rasim Delic, with our assistant, Lejla Gluhic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Good afternoon to you, sir. May the witness please take the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- make the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Delalic. You may take your seat.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What position did you hold before the witness?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Before the war, I was a commander of a squad of the Military Police in Sabac. It's a military duty. The ranks are from the military branch.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner, would it perhaps be helpful just to get the names of the witness on record before we carry on, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you please tell your name, Witness?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Asim Delalic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: When was your place of birth, and where were you born?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: 10th of December in 1955 in Suhi Dol, near Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Coming back to your the Military police, what training did you receive with the Military Police?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: I didn't have military police training. I completed training for a squad commander of the infantry. And as one of the disciplined commanders, when I was transferred to Sabac, I became the commander of the military police squad there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Having been Commander of the Military Police, what is the first step which is to be performed if the Military Police captures a prisoner of war in the field?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: If the Military Police arrests a prisoner of war in the field, then they are supposed to secure him and also search him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Search him for what?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Search for weapons, if he's armed. Of course, it's not going to take with them an armed person.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: When the war in Bosnia started, what unit did you join?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: At the beginning, I was in the Suhi Dol Company, at the beginning when the defence was formed in relation to the Serbian and Montenegrin aggressor. And on the 7th of May, 1992, with Mr. Zijad Selman, who came to pick me up, I went to Travnik, to the Military Police, where a military police company was being formed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And thereafter, after being at the Military Police in Travnik, what unit did you join, if any?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: On my personal request, I returned to Mehurici, where the Mehuric Detachment was formed, which took the place of the Regional Staff before that, and that's where I was appointed Commander of the Military Police Squad there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: When was this?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: This was in late September 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And where were you based?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: We were based in the Mehurici Elementary School, on the ground floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Which other unit did you join thereafter?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: As the units became larger, and with the creation of brigades and corps, we moved to the 306th Mountain Brigade where the Mehurici Detachment also moved to.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What position did you hold there?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: I was appointed Assistant Commander for Security.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Who was your superior within the 306th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: My superior was the commander along the command -- line of command. According to the Counter-Intelligence chain of command, it was the Chief of Security of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: When and where did you first meet a Mujahedin during your tenure in the 306th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: The first time I came to Mehurici, I encountered a certain group that was based on the second floor or billeted on the second floor of the elementary school.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: How large was that group?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: I said that I don't know. They were often on the move. It was hard to count them, so that I really wouldn't want to just make an estimation or a guess offhand.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And when did you first see them?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: This was in late September when I came to Mehurici.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Which year?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: As a commander of the Military Police Squad in -- from September 1992, how did you consider the presence of Mujahedin from a security perspective?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: I wasn't a commander of the platoon, but I was a squad commander. At the time, they didn't present any danger to us. They were involved in some sort of humanitarian work, so we didn't really pay that much attention to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And how long did you hold this view that they -- that you didn't need to pay attention to them?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Up until April 1993, when the Miletic thing happened, until then.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What do you refer to by "Miletic thing" or "Miletici thing"?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: It's generally known that five civilians were killed there and that the entire Croatian population and the Bosniak population that tried to protect them was taken to their base in Savica Kuce, where they were located regardless of ethnicity. They had the same behaviour towards the Croats and the Bosniaks who tried to protect them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you just clarify, you were referring to "they." Whom do you mean by "they?"

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: The Mujahedin who did this infamous or dishonourable act.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I wish to show you a document, PT1085.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: We need page 2 of the English and of B/C/S version. This document, for your information, was sent by Esad Sipic, the commander of the 306th Brigade, and the last paragraph on page 2 in both versions, says, and I will quote: "Soldiers of other units, 'Mr. Sipic writes,' who have gotten out of line with their security commands represent a security problem of particular concern in our zone of responsibility." And if the B/C/S version could please be moved to page 3, and the English as well, there is, in the first line of the B/C/S, an attack -- or Miletici mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Is that the incident we just discussed? In the English version, it's the second paragraph of page 3, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: I don't know what Commander Sipic meant when he drafting this document, but Miletici happened just once, it wasn't repeated.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So this document dates from the 5th of May. When was the incident in Miletici happening?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: The incident in Miletici, I'm not sure exactly when it happened, but I think it was the 24th of April, from what I can recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I wish to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 254.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I wish to show you another document, PT1087. We see here, on the first page of the B/C/S version, that this is a security bulletin from the Supreme Command Staff, dating from the 8th of May, 1993, so three days after the document of Mr. Sipic. And I'm interested in the third page of both B/C/S and English versions, and it mentions in the second paragraph of the B/C/S here along an attack on the village of Miletici. In the English, it's the third paragraph. Do you see this?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I cannot see. I forgot my glasses, so now I have problems when I have to read.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I could read you the relevant -- I mean, I wanted to show a couple of documents to this witness, so I'm --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Could his glasses be retrieved from the waiting room?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Are your glasses in the waiting room?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are you able to lead the witness on other aspects which do not need reading in the meantime?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I only had one question to this document --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I only had one question to this document. I wanted to ask the witness whether the information, as provided by Commander Sipic, had reached the Security Administration of the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: For him to answer that question, he must read the document, so that's a question that requires his glasses. Are there questions that do not require -- things that he can answer from memory without looking at the page?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: This paragraph also mentions that Serb families from Mehurici have been expelled, so I just quote. Two Serb families from their family house in the village of Mehurici are mentioned, and it is mentioned that Ramo Durmis moved into their house houses. My question to you, Witness, is: You already mentioned the Savica houses. Are these the Serb houses mentioned in which Ramo Durmis moved into?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Savici Kuce is inhabited by Serbs, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And if you can look at the document, it states, in the same paragraph, the second paragraph of this document in front of you, that Ramo Durmis moved into their houses. Can you confirm this?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that information. Ramo Durmis was not a member of the 306th Mountain Brigade, and I think that we did furnish a document confirming that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Confirming what?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: That he was not a member of the 306th Mountain Brigade. I don't know whether he moved into Savica Kuce or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Looking at the paragraph now, you see that Miletici -- the information about the attack on Miletici has reached, indeed, the Supreme Command Security Administration. Can you confirm at least this?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: I can't confirm that because I did not investigate the Miletici incident. I did not consider Miletici to be my area of responsibility. And from what I can remember, the investigation was conducted there by a joint commission comprising the 3rd Corps, the UNPROFOR, and the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Sorry, I'm asking you only whether the information, which we have seen in the previous document from Commander Sipic, has reached the Security Administration of the Supreme Command as you may see here in this document, whether you could confirm this.

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: I can see the document in front of me, but I don't know if it reached the Security Administration. If they received the document, then those who did receive it would be able to tell you if they did so.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: But if you look at the first page again, it's a document from the Security Administration, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is the witness looking at the first page? Is the first page up yet?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can we please switch to the first page? Yes, here.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you confirm that this, indeed, is from the Security Administration of the General Staff?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Sir, I did not have a document like this in my hands when I was in the army. Documents like this did not reach me, so I cannot confirm if this is that document or not. I can see that it is the Supreme Command Staff Security Administration document, but we didn't receive documents of this type.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can I at least mark the document for identification?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted for identification. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be MFI 255.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Did you ever visit the Savici Kuce?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: No, only once when I was there, but they didn't allow us to enter to speak with the Mujahedin commander regarding the Miletici problem. I didn't enter the houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What did the Mujahedin commander tell you about the Miletici problem?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: My commander, Mr. Sipic, wanted to find out more after the incident that happened there, and he asked me to go and -- with him and talk to them. And when we got to the gate, a guard was there. He was an Arab, and he didn't know the language, so we managed to understand each other somehow, that we wanted to reach the person in charge. But he wouldn't let us pass. He blew into a whistle and two men came out of the house. One of them, I think, was a Bosniak and the other was an Arab, so we assumed that that was the person in charge, although I didn't know him. And when we were talking with them to see how we could surmount the problems, he said that there was nothing to talk about with us, that he was in contact with Mr. Sefer Halilovic, they were forming the 8th Muslim Brigade, and that they did not wish to talk with us at all. And that's when we ended our meeting. They didn't allow us to go inside.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can Exhibit 136 please be shown.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Is this the document which relates to your visit you just described?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Moving on, you mentioned the forming of the 8th Muslim Brigade. What happened to some soldiers of the 306th Brigade when the Mujahedin attempted to form their unit?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Some soldiers --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, just a second. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is an extremely leading question. First of all, he has to establish that something had happened, and then he can move on. I haven't heard so far that anything had happened to the soldiers of the 306th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Mr. Delalic, you mentioned in page 11, line 3, that the Mujahedin claimed to form the 8th Muslim Brigade. What effect, if any, did the alleged forming of this 8th Muslim Brigade have on 306th Brigade soldiers?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: In the first place, was the 8th Muslim Brigade formed?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I rephrase that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Did the Mujahedin form the 8th Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: No, they did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What formation, if any, could be accomplished by the Mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Well, they didn't have enough personnel to establish a brigade, probably, but they did have a number of Bosniaks who had crossed over to them. We call these people the Muslim Forces, but they were not within any one of the brigades that was in the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina in that period. In order to establish the 8th Muslim Brigade, it was our assessment that the 306th Brigade would have to be broken up, and that was very important for us for safeguarding the area in the valley.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You mentioned that Bosniaks crossed over to them, to the Mujahedin. From which units did they cross over?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Well, usually from all units, but quite a few went from the 306th Brigade, in terms of what we had there, there were about 50 or 40 persons. In the initial stage, as far as I can remember, Ramo Durmis was the leader of the Bosniaks with the Mujahedin.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I wish to show you PT1440, a document from the 2nd of August, 1993, and I'm particularly interested, after the first page has been shown, in the list attached to this document. This should be the next pages. I think it's one further. There is a list. I think it's the very last page. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If you please look at this list, and my question to you is whether these soldiers are from the 306th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I wish to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 256.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I wish to show you now document PT1480, a document from three weeks later 20th August, 1993. A document authored by Mr. Ahmed Adilovic, and it has also a list attached. I'm just interested in the list for the time being. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If you could please look at the list and tell us whether these are soldiers from the 306th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, there are quite a few soldiers from this list who left the 306th Brigade, but there are some who left before the 306th Brigade had been established, so therefore had not been in the 306th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And these people -- okay. But you recognise the majority of these people; yeah?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: I don't know -- well, I know about 30 per cent of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can I please tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 257.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I wish to move on to another section dealing with combat with the HVO at the beginning of June 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Where have you been in late May, early June, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Late in May and the beginning of June 1993, I was at the Basic Command Post at Rudnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: This is the Basic Command Post of the 306th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Where was your commander at that time?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Well, the situation itself on the ground, the Bilanska [phoen] Valley, was broken up into four or five entities. The commander, with part of his assistant commanders, was in the village of Krpeljici.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And how was the situation there?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Well, the situation was very difficult, you know. We could not communicate with anybody. The Basic Command Post in Rudnik was encircled for about 20 days, and it was shelled all the time. The commander, with part of his assistant commanders, was in Krpeljici, and they were also encircled. They could not even go anywhere. Some were in Han Bila encircled as well with the commander of the 3rd Battalion. They couldn't go anywhere, either. Part of the Basic Command Post of Rudnik was cut off. Ali Hodja and the rest. I think that the assistant commander for replenishment was there, and he couldn't get anywhere, either. So the situation was really difficult.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: How was the situation solved for Commander Sipic in Krpeljici?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Well, the factual situation at the time was that the HVO controlled the dominant features, and also they had put up check-points and we couldn't move about. The first thing that happened was that they presented an ultimatum to the village of Letici, which was behind Brankovac and Cifluk down there, told them to move out, to hand over their weapons and move out, which is what they did the end of May, beginning of June, I think. The second thing that happened was that on the 4th of June, in 1993, an ultimatum was presented to Velika Bukovica to hand over their weapons and move out. They did not agree to that, and the HVO immediately starting -- started hitting them. The fighting went on for two days until the HVO managed to place under their control the village of Velika Bukovica. In that period we were receiving alarming news at the Basic Command Post, although communication was difficult. Radio communications were used. The last thing we heard was that there were 18 dead and 6 wounded, as far as I can remember. We sent this telegram further on to our commander, and that required action for deblocking and Velika Bukovica. The commander sent a telegram up there to Mehurici asking for a deblockade of Velika Bukovica to be carried out. That's sometime around the 6th, I think, that he asked for this, for the action to start on the 7th. But at that moment, our forces were not ready for that. Following these telegrams at the Basic Command Post, my estimate was that the action could start on the 8th, which is indeed what happened, the 8th, and the 9th the situation was resolved. Velika Bukovica was deblocked.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Via which way from Mehurici was Velika Bukovica deblocked?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: I was at the Basic Command Post. I could not follow this. But during my first testimony, I said that our forces, I don't know what strength it was, left from Suhi Dol and Mehurici. That is what I heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: In which direction?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Well, towards Maline and Velika Bukovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I wish to show you document PT1852, a document entitled "Report and Proposal of the Bosanska Krajina", and this report and proposal is made to the 3rd Corps. And if you please only look at the second-last paragraph from the bottom, yes. It says here it has been ordered -- if the English could be moved down a little bit, please. Thank you. I think on the English it's page 2, actually, the third paragraph. Yes, you can stop here: "It has been ordered," the third paragraph says, that "Esad Sipic should, organise one battalion strong unit (300 men) from the part of the 306th BBL and from residence of the village of Mehurici to move on the axis, the village of Maline, the village of Radonjici, the village of Krpeljici." Is that what you just described, what happened on the 8th of June?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: I haven't seen this document. I cannot make any comments regarding that document. I don't think that Commander Sipic had received this document, either. He couldn't have.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: But reading the document now, does that not confirm what you just told us, that from Mehurici troops moved via Maline towards Krpeljici? That's my only question.

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: They were moving towards Velika Bukovica, not towards Krpeljici, because Krpeljici had a Bosniak population.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can I tender this document into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 258.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Was, in the course of the 8th June combat activities you just described, happening anything of a security concern?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: On the 8th of June -- I mean I was at the Basic Command Post up until the 11th of June at Rudnik. When I came to Mehurici, I saw that in the school there was a large number of refugees. Actually, that is where they were protected, in a way. Part of the military-aged persons were also staying in part of Kovacnice [phoen]. I found out from my desk officer -- I went to see him immediately, and he told me that part of them -- well, he wasn't so sure. I think he said that part of them had been abducted by the Military Police of the 1st Battalion that was in charge of these persons. When I came to Mehurici, then this was confirmed to me by Mr. Zukanovic, who was the Assistant Commander for Security Affairs of the 1st Battalion; namely, that 20 to 25 people had been abducted and that they were missing, totally.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And did you manage to establish the fate of these 20 to 25 missing?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Well, the commander scheduled a meeting of the Command on the 12th of June in Krpeljici. We were there, the corps of the Command, that is, and I said that there were some indications to the effect that these people had been killed, perhaps, and I ordered Hasan Zukanovic to carry out an investigation, a full investigation, as to how this happened, who the perpetrator was, et cetera. I immediately reported to the superior command about this, and 15 days later the investigations that I had at that point showed that the perpetrators were the Mujahedin, that there weren't any members who -- members of the 306th Brigade that were involved in this, and I informed about the investigation the Security Command of the 3rd Corps, and by virtue of that fact I could not continue investigating because in that period no one could enter the Mujahedin camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: In the course of the investigation you just mentioned, were the bodies of the 20 to 25 persons inspected?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: As for the sanitization of the terrain, as far as I learned, it was carried out by the Civil Protection on the 9th, immediately, between Bikosi-Maline. The so-called Pjescara, as far as I know, that was not looked at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, just a clarification with the witness. There has been a misinterpretation. It says here on page 21 that part of them, meaning these people, had been abducted by the Military Police of the 1st Battalion, so it sounds as if it's the Military Police that had abducted of the 1st Battalion, but the witness actually said something different, that they had been abducted from the Military Police, if I understood it correctly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, you're referring us to page 21. According to my screen, I'm still on page 19. Let me see if --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry. Page 17, line 19 through 21.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Would you like to verify that with the witness, Mr. Neuner?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, the 20 to 25 persons, from whom were these people abducted?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: The Military Police of the 1st Battalion of the 306th Brigade was taking all of these people, civilians and military-age men, towards -- and it was the Mujahedin, with masked persons, who had abducted them, unknown persons to this day. It is assumed these persons were Bosniaks who were with the Mujahedin.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. I want to now ask for a clarification of what you said earlier about the Civil Protection. You said on the 9th they sanitised the Teha [phoen]. Are you referring to the 9th of June, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And then it says, it is almost disappearing in the transcript, "the so-called Pjescara"? Can you clarify what you meant by this? They were sanitizing, and then you said something about Pjescara?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: They picked up the bodies, dead bodies, that is sanitization of the area, and they buried them in Pescara, the locality of Pjescara.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Had you ever been at that location?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Well, I passed by that location. I wasn't there. I wasn't born too far away from that place.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: When did you pass by that location, please?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Well, I passed there during the war, after the war, before the war, whatever.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Did you pass by that location after the bodies had been buried there by the Civil Protection?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Not immediately, because I had a lot of work in the brigade and on the terrain, along the defence lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Did you pass by later?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Well, I cannot remember when I passed after that because, really, I used a vehicle to go out to the terrain, but maybe two or three months later I passed by.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: This would be, then, the month of October?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: I cannot remember exactly. I have said this officially now, two or three months after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What did you observe two or three months later in Pjescara?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Well, look, this is a terrain where sand was taken out of the ground, and it was not my job to see how people were being buried and in what way. Why they were not buried at the cemetery, the Civilian Protection dealt with that, and it's best for you to ask them why it was that they buried them there. I was not there, as a matter of fact, when the terrain was sanitized.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Did anybody of your Military Security Service ever look at the bodies before or after they were buried?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: I don't think that they had time to look at them, because Zukanovic came around the 10th. He was in hospital in Zenica, and they brought him there ill on the 10th in Mehurici, and I'm saying that the bodies had been buried by them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Were these bodies ever exhumed?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And did anybody from your Military Security Service look at these bodies after they were exhumed?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: I don't know. Nobody asked us for anything like that, and as far as I recall, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And when were they exhumed?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: I don't know that, either.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Was, after the completion of the investigation, ever a criminal report filed about what was learned by your service through the investigation?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: All the information we had, compiled by Mr. Zukanovic, who was a policeman before the war, I think if you believe that we were that capable, I'm going to say that we weren't actually, but he was an active military policeman, he worked as such. So whatever he compiled we forwarded it to the Security Administration of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: In the form of a criminal report?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: He took statements on the record from military policemen, and then later he put everything on paper, together with an official note, saying that the outcome of the investigation was that no participants or perpetrators belonged to the 306th Brigade, and we didn't know who the perpetrators were. And as far as we were concerned, we did not -- or we were unable to have any further influence on the further course of the investigation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, again a matter of translation. Page 22, lines, I think, 3 and 4, the witness said: "We wrote who did that," and in the transcript it says: "We did not know who did it." So we would just like to have that clarified with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You heard what my learned colleague said. Did you wrote who was the perpetrator of the crime at Bikosi?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: We said that it was indisputable that the act was committed by the Mujahedin unit, which in that period, was not under the control of the Army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want to show you document PT1423 from the 24th of July, 1993. It's a protest from the 306th Brigade. My first question -- okay, there are a couple of names listed here in this document, and in the text it says that criminal reports had been filed. Were these - that's my only question - the criminal reports filed by your Military Security Service at that point in time, meaning the 24th of July, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: This is our protest. It's our document, the Military Security Administration, and I think it referred to the fact that the District Military Prosecutor from Travnik gave information that they received only one criminal report from the 306th Mountain Brigade. And then based on that information, Mr. Haris Jusic drafted this document and provided the numbers and the dates when the criminal reports were submitted, as well as the names of the persons. It was a matter of 11 criminal reports that were submitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Filed until the 24th of July, 1993, by your Military Security Service; correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I wish to tender that document into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 259.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want to take you to October 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: My first question is: You said earlier 15 days after you learned about the incident in Bikosi in June, the investigation was completed. Was the investigation ever reopened into the Bikosi events?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: From what I can remember, I don't think that it was, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: How long did you remain with the 306th Military Security Service?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Until the 14th of February, 1996, when I was demobilised upon my personal request.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Until then, was your Service ever investigating again or reopening an investigation into the Bikosi events from June 1993?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: No, because we believed that we had no authority over the perpetrators of this act.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Have you ever seen a letter drafted for you in October 1993 which referred to the events in Bikosi on the 8th of June, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If Exhibit 140 may please be shown to this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You see the document here. Have you ever seen that document?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: In the testimony -- my testimony in 2005, I saw this document for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I can see that the document is signed for you. How was the procedure at the time when documents are signed for you?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: All the documents sent to the Superior Command that was of importance was signed by me. Official notes were signed by the person who had drafted the official notes, because they were responsible for the accuracy of the data, while criminal reports were signed by Mr. Haris Jusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: This is a report here, as the title says. How was the procedure if somebody in your service signs a report for you?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: I would happen to be away several times, because I was also obliged to go to the Forward Command Post. If I wasn't there, then somebody had to sign the documents of urgency in my stead. I did not sign this document, and I didn't see it until 2005.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: On the 19th of October, when this document is signed, October 1993, where have you been?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: I was most probably at the Forward Command Post.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What Forward Command Post are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Our Forward Command Post was at Parica Greda at Mount Vlasic that was facing the Serbian-Montenegrin aggressor.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Is that the only forward command post of the 306th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: In that period, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: From when to when did you stay at this Forward Command Post?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: It would usually last for a week, and then after that you would get a day or two of rest. Sometimes it would be even longer, depending on the situation in the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So your answer today is -- how long did you stay there?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: At least nine days.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I have a diary entry for you. This is PT1020A. It's a diary of the 306th Mountain Brigade. While this is being shown, can I ask you: Have you ever seen General Alagic at the IKM?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: On Vlasic, Parica Greda, I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If we scroll down here in the B/C/S version of the document, and in the English it should please be the second page, this is an entry relating to 1600 hours on the 17th of October. It's the last entry. It says here at 1600 hours there was a briefing with the Bosanska Krajina commander in the IKM. Do you recall that meeting, since you were at the IKM of the 306th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: I cannot remember. That was a long time ago and it was a long period. There were various meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I wish to tender the document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, first of all, I don't see the basis for tendering this document. Secondly, I would like to ask my learned friends from the Prosecutors, so that we could follow the proceedings, first to receive excerpts from the diary, because we just get numbers with a large number of pages and then it's very difficult to follow. We cannot locate what the Prosecutor is asking questions about. I've encountered this problem several times before. A diary numbering several hundred pages, and then I cannot know what the point of the questioning is, and it's hard for us then to prepare for cross-examination in view of this particular problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, would it be okay for you to ask questions -- to object while seated. If you would just like to switch on your light, you can object while seated, in line with your request the other day. Thank you very much. Mr. Neuner, are you able to answer that? As there was quite a number of points raised in that objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I can say the Prosecution faced the same situation, in a way, that we ourselves had to dig through this diary, which as my learned colleague says, has a number of pages, and we ourselves had only certain pages translated to this point. And I, myself, have learned, through a proofing which took place relatively recently, meaning yesterday, that the witness stated he was at this IKM. So it was only yesterday, in the course of the afternoon, that we, ourselves, learned that this date was indeed of relevance, and we just went again to access this lengthy document after what we had learned from the witness. We have tried to make a very timely disclosure of the proofing note yesterday to our learned colleagues, and I can say I was in the same footing as my learned colleague for this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Now, there is no objection to the tendering of the document, but there is no basis for the tendering. Do you have any response to that?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'm prepared to ask Mr. Delalic about the cover of the 306th Mountain Brigade war diary and whether he can, in general, acknowledge that this is the diary which was used at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. You do have questions to ask to the witness to establish the basis. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: We have now isolated this one page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: How long are you going to be with establishing the basis?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I think two minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Two minutes?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If the usher could assist, please, just having the PT number 1020 displayed. This is just one page we isolated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is it 1020 or 1020A?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: This is 1020A, and this is an excerpt taken out of this longer war diary. We didn't want to tender the entire war diary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: To save time, the Prosecution would even have a hard copy of the cover page here. Okay, it's already on the e-court, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you remember the cover page of this, Mr. Delalic?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: This diary was at the Basic Command Post.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Of the 306th Brigade, you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So if I would say that we have isolated the one page I showed to you earlier out of this diary, would you think that this is an authentic piece from the war diary used at the time by your brigade?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: The duty officers would write the entries, so I don't know what to say about that. Not -- there wasn't one person that was maintaining the war diary. All the compiled information and data would be entered into the diary.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If you look again at the entry from the 17th of October, does that look like the war diary used at the time by the 306th Mountain Brigade? If we could please have PT1020A shown.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could the Prosecutors put factual questions that are in the diary and not this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We're now five minutes beyond the time for a break. Do you think you can carry on with this basis laying when we come back?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We'll come back at 4.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just before we went for the break, Madam Vidovic was suggesting that you ask factual questions to establish the basis for tendering the document. Do you have any response to that, Mr. Neuner?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Mr. Delalic, can you explain how these war diaries of the 306th were compiled at the time?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Well, I've already said that the war diary was done by the duty officer on the basis of information collected from the field for that particular day.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And where would the duty operations officer sit?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Well, at the Basic Command Post. I don't know now, was it in Guca Gora or was it -- no, I think it was at Guca Gora.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: On that basis, Your Honour, I would like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 260.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I have another question relating to the October events. Could the document PT-1589 please be shown. This is in response from the 3rd Corps, Mr. Delalic, dating the 21st of October. And in the B/C/S version we would be interested in the last line of that document. In the English, it's the second page and the second line there. We discussed this a moment ago. It talks here about Pjescara. You mentioned at this location. It says here: "A total of 25 soldiers and civilians were collected in one spot and buried in two graves between the villages (illegible) and Maline at the place known as Pjescara." This relates to the Bikosi events. And if we could go at the end of this document, meaning in the B/C/S, it would be the next page, to the second-last paragraph of the document. It says here, in the first line: "The Assistant Commander for Security from the 306th Brigade visited the location ..." Do you remember having visited Pjescara in October 1993, as the document alleges?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you believe you have visited it earlier or later?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: I did not go to Pjescara with anyone to see it. I passed by it myself when I was going home.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And when was this? This document is from the 21st of October, 1993.

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: I already mentioned, two or three months after that I took a shortcut to my village where I lived.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Two or three months after what, please?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Well, after those events in Maline.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So two or three months. This would be August or September 1993; yeah?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could the document at least be marked for identification, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document should be marked for identification. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be MFI 261.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I come to my -- excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, may I? This document has already been admitted into evidence as D231, but in a more legible version. Exhibit 231.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now, was it Exhibit 231 or was it D231? And you may remain seated.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Exhibit 231.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you accept that, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Certainly. An oversight by our side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay, thank you very much. Then the document has already been admitted as an exhibit, and it may not -- it need not be marked for identification any longer. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I come to my last line of questions relating to combat operations of the 306th Brigade. Mr. Delalic, I wish to show you PT1539. This is again an entry in the war diary of the 306th Brigade, this time from the 9th of September, and I'm interested in the last sentence. It says here: "The Commander of the OG Bosanska Krajina and a representative of the El Mujahedin visited our Command." Do you recall that event?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I wish to leave the document marked for identification, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the document be marked for identification. May it be given an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is will be MFI 261.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You want to say something?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: If I could see here that in that period I was visiting the 1st Mountain Battalion with Mr. Husic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes. Do you recall this?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Well, look, 15 years is a long time. I cannot remember everything, so I cannot remember whether commander of the OG Bosanska Krajina received the representatives or what -- whatever.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: But do you recall your visit to the 1st Brigade or 1st Battalion?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Well, look, every day we went -- well, if I were to remember each and every individual thing that happened, I would be the biggest computer in the world.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I leave it here and move on to the next exhibit, which dates a day later, the 10th of September, 1993, PT1542, a report by the 306th Mountain Brigade to the OG Bosanska Krajina. We would need the first page of the B/C/S, and the end of the second paragraph is relevant for Mr. Delalic, and in the English it's the first page at the end, running into then the second page. I would just read out the, to save time, the relevant portion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Indeed. You're left with about four minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes. "Our units," it says,"In coordination with the 325th Brigade and the El Mujahedin detachment took some positions previously held by the HVO units." My question to you is: Do you know where Djotline Kuce is located?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: It is possible that our units acted there in concert, but El Mujahedin never functioned under the command of the 306th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: My question to you was whether you know where Djotline Kuce is, the location mentioned. That's all I want to know.

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Djotline Kuce, I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Where is it, where is this?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Somewhere in the area of the Vitez Municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: We should tender this document into evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 262.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The last document is from the 28th of July, PT1430, again a document of the 306th Mountain Brigade. We need, from the B/C/S version, page 1. The beginning of the last main paragraph, if you would please look at this. This is a document from Halim Husic, and in the English version page 2, the beginning of the last main paragraph on page 2, please. And I'm reading out the relevant portion: "In Hrasce, (688), where the latest offensive conducted by our forces failed. Our forces tried several times, but it was unsuccessful like this time." Could you tell us where Hrasce the location is located, please?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: I know Hrasce as 688, Feature 688, but as far as I know, even before the fighting started in the area of Velika Bukovica and afterwards, it was in the hands of the HVO, and it was a dominant feature at that. From there, they -- they opened sniper fire at our lines all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: How far away from Guca Gora is this Hrasce location, roughly?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Well, I cannot say exactly. Perhaps a kilometre to a kilometre and a half.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I would like to tender this document into evidence, and I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before we do that, I have a small question for the witness. Witness, that very sentence that was read by counsel, it says: "In Hrasce (688), where the latest offensive conducted by our forces failed, 17," and then "314, Mujahedin and our forces tried the same several times ..." Now, did at any stage the Mujahedin and your forces fight side by side? This is what seems to be suggested by that sentence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think they didn't in this area. As far as I know, in this area, with our unit, the El Mujahed Unit never fought together with our unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Did the El Mujahedin ever fight with your unit at any other time at any other place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Possibly, somewhere there may have been cooperation, but it certainly never fought under the command of the 306th Brigade. That is what I state here categorically.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And that I understood. All I want to find out is whether they fought side by side with each other at any stage during the war. You have answered that. You said, yes, they probably had. They were in cooperation with you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Possibly, possibly at Djotline Kuce, but I don't know of them cooperating with us, acting in concert with us, anywhere.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Any cross-examination, Madam Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I just ask that the document be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I beg your pardon. The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 263.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Madam Vidovic. You may remain seated, Madam.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Cross-examination by Madam Vidovic:

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'm Vasvija Vidovic, and I'm going to be putting questions to you today on behalf of the Defence of General Rasim Delic. Cross-examination, by its very nature, means that you can give "yes" or "no" answers to most of my questions, unless you feel it is necessary to clarify something or if the Honourable Trial Chamber asks you to do that. Since there are many questions, I kindly ask you to give "yes" or "no" whenever possible. Have you understood me?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: One more thing, one more thing. We speak the same language. I will do my best, and you please do your best to pause between question and answer so that the transcript would record the answers. Have you understood me?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You told us that you were born in the village of Suhi Dol, Municipality of Travnik and that that's where you grew up, too?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You completed a secondary school for printers; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You did not complete any police course, or did you do any kind of police work before the war; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: No, I did not complete any police course, but I was leader of a squad of the Military Police in the former Yugoslav Peoples Army, as I've already mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes. So this was a course for squad leaders in the infantry; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: It was your testimony that at the beginning of the war, you were in a military police company of the municipal headquarters of the Territorial Defence; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: In that period, the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina did not have rules for the work of the Military Police; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: It didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What you did was bringing into custody persons who had not responded to call-ups, mobilisation?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You provided security for buildings?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: In actual fact that is the experience that you had as a military policeman from the Territorial Defence Staff?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You were Assistant Commander for Security in the detachment of the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: When the 306th Brigade was established, you assumed duty of the Assistant for Security of that brigade; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Not in a single one of these two stages of your military service were you professionally trained to work in military security?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The officers who are supposed to work in military security of the brigade, according to establishment, should have university degrees; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: They should be officers with a completed military academy, the security stream; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: As for Assistant Commander for Security, according to the rules that were in force in the Army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and in other armies, too, a brigadier or a colonel should hold that position; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: These rules were adopted in the autumn of 1992. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: In 1993, in Biljanska Dolina, you quite simply did not have such officers; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: We didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Other persons in the 306th Brigade, in the Security Organ, did not have professional knowledge from the field of security; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: They didn't have them?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: They didn't have them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Commander of the Platoon of the 306th Brigade, Sabanovic Suad, he was also not trained for that duty?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: He wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: In your work, you cooperated with the civilian police in Mehurici; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The civilian police was in charge of protecting civilians during the war and their property; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The civilian police in Mehurici was also poorly armed and poorly equipped, like the army; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: They did not have enough long rifles; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Only a few?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Now I'm going to ask you something briefly about the situation in the Travnik area. After the conflict in Novi Travnik in October 1992, the HVO established a line vis a vis the Muslim villages; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The forces of the HVO did that also in the area of Maline towards the village of Suhi Dol and that's where you're from, where you were born?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would now have the witness look at Exhibit P98. For the transcript, before the witness sees the document, I would like to say that this is a document of the 306th Brigade of the 11th of April, 1993, entitled "Report by the Security Organ." This is D98.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, is this an exhibit or is it a "D98" document?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's D98, Your Honour. It's still not an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's just that you're calling it an Exhibit D98, so call it "document D98".

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, I'm going to quote only a small excerpt from this document, the first sentence of this document, which states: "According to latest information, we have obtained information that an HVO/Croatian Defence Council/brigade is being formed in our zone of responsibility with the Brigade Command Post in the village of Guca Gora. The name of the brigade is the Frankopan, the brigade commander is Ilija Nakic." And then a little bit lower, the command post, Your Honours, it's somewhere in the middle of the third paragraph, it says, the command post of the second reserve battalion is in the village of Guca Gora and it covers right -- the ground on the left bank of the Bila River and it represents the villages: Guca Gora, Velika Bukovica, Radonjici, Maline, Podstinje, Pokrajcici, and Sarici." In relation to this document, witness, the Frankopan Brigade covered the area of the villages mentioned in this document including Maline; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could this document please be admitted and given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 264.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: In mid-April 1992, and you confirmed this in response to a question by the Prosecutor, the Bila area was blocked by the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would just like the witness to look at D220, please. It's a report by the 306th Brigade of the 13th of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, please, can you look at the part of the document under "3" just below the title: "HVO." I'm going to read a small excerpt: "It has been established that a large number of HVO members stationed in the villages are people from outside. New check-points have been set up, and the old ones in the usual places have been fortified: The Han Bila-Zenica road at Ovnak, the Rudnik-Nova Bila above Pokrajcici, Rudnik-Goca Gora on Mount Kosovo, and several check-points outside on the Guca-Gora Travnik road." I would just like to ask you whether this document attests correctly to the situation that was in the field at that time?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Is it true that the HVO, in the course of April 1993, brought in a lot of people to the area who were not from there, they were from the outside; are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I would just like you to look further down on the page of this document. Actually, in the English version it's on page 2, and it has to do with communications. It's the last sentence in the first paragraph, which states: "Communications and the security of communications with Travnik are also poor and unreliable. The situation is not improving regarding communications with the OG West Command, Bugojno, so observations made in previous reports still apply." Do you agree that at the time that communications were poor and unreliable between your brigade and Travnik as well as the Command in Bugojno?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: This situation lasted until your area was unblocked in June 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, can this document please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit number 265.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, in connection to answers the witness gave to questions by the Prosecutor regarding the village of Velika Bukovica linked to the events of the 8th of April, I would like to place this map on the ELMO showing the area of the Bila region.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, I am going to ask you to find Velika Bukovica and circle it, please. I think that perhaps it's to the left. And in the lower left-hand corner, you can see it, Witness, if I may assist you, and all you need to do is to point it out for the Trial Chamber, and if you can circle it.

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And you can see Velika Bukovica there and Mala Bukovica. That's the area. Can you please circle that, please?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And I'm going to ask you also to point out to the Trial Chamber the area of Hajdareve Njive. It's near Travnik, that place is near Travnik. You can allow us to see Travnik. That's right. And can you please help us and indicate where that is?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: This part and then this part [indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: This is called Hajdareve Njive?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Can you circle that, and, please, can you circle where you indicated, Witness, and since you cannot see it on the map --

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes. Can you also write down in your own writing the words "Hajdareve Njive"?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: On the side or here [indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: There, there, Hajdareve Njive?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, thank you. Your Honours, could this map be given an exhibit number, please? Perhaps it could be photographed electronically, if possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The map is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit number 266.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. And now, in respect of Velika Bukovica, I'm going to ask you some questions. I would like the witness to look at D222, please. For the transcript, it's D222. This is a report of the 306th Brigade Security Service, and it bears the date the 28th of June, 1993.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, the 26th of June, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And if you can look at the introductory paragraph stating: "Made on the 26th of May, 1993, in the village of Velika Bukovica, in respect to the attack of the HVO units on this village on the 4th of April, 1993, and taking the Muslims" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Slow down, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. So it's a record made on the 26th of June, 1993, in the village of Velika Bukovica, in respect to the attack of the HVO units on this village on the 4th of June, 1993, and taking the Muslims to the prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I would like to ask you the following: This is a document drafted by your security organ; do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And I would just like you to look at a small excerpt of this document, which states on the first day, somewhere in the middle of the page -- let's just see where it is in the English version. It begins with the words: "On the first day ..." It's towards the end of the page. Very well: "On the first day of the attack, seven members of the armija were killed as follows:" And then they're named. And then: "On the 8th of June, 1993, HVO soldiers took all of us who stayed alive from the village, total number of 88 people, to Konjska to be used as human shields."

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What I would like to ask you is this: Konjska is a part of the Skradno village in the Bukovica Municipality; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Konjska is on a plateau above Velika Bukovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: All right, very well. Did you have information that these people were taken to the village of Skradno in the Bukovica Municipality?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: We had information that they were first taken to Nova Bila, where a large number of the young women were abused in a dishonourable way, and then after that they were taken down towards Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: All right. So then they were taken to the area of Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can this document be given an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 267.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I showed this document because of Exhibit 170, so can we now have Exhibit 170, which is under seal, and perhaps we can move into private session because of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are now in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, now I'd like to ask you something about the 306th Brigade, and could you look at Exhibit 142, please. For the transcript, this is a document of the Command of the 306th Brigade. It seems that it was signed by the witness, and I would like the witness to have a look at it. That's fine, thank you. Witness, you can see the document. Can you recognise this document, or do you want us to have a look at page 2 as well? Please, anyway, can we have the document moved so that we see where the signature is?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If you look at the document, it indicates what problems follow the establishment of the 306th Brigade in January; am I right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
