utterances.text: And I see that you said here the leaderships of the local persons who held meetings and promised zones of responsibility. Could you tell us, quite briefly, what did you mean by this, "leadership of local persons," what did you mean?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Well, individuals who -- well, the 306th Brigade could not be formed at all, and they were making it disintegrate. They were promising the peasants that they would be able to hold lines only above their own villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. In relation to this question, I just wonder whether I understood what you were saying. These were people outside the military; right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Who were these people; can you tell us?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Well, one of these people was Hadzira, Puric, Mira, I think was his name. While the 306th Brigade was being established, some villages seceded from it and joined the 314th Brigade. They didn't want to be with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Then you indicated that at least two brigades did not respect the corps order to take over the zone of responsibility on the 8th of January; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And then you pointed out that the soldiers in the field were not sufficiently informed?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Now I'd like to ask you the following: Please, it is correct, is it not, that the situation did not get any better over the following months?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: We constantly had to deal with a difficult situation, because from starters we were given a very big area of responsibility facing the Serb-Montenegrin aggressor. We were poorly armed, poorly equipped, there was a lack of discipline, and if we look at all of that, these were the problems that our brigade had to face.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Please, is it correct that after the blockade of the area in mid-April 1993, the situation the brigade, and in the corps, became even more difficult?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Well, by virtue of the fact that the brigade, when it already started functioning, had to face these conflicts and it was broken into four or five entities --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you, thank you, you've already explained that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could this document please be removed now, and could the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] Been removed?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Exhibit 254 shown to him by the Prosecutor today, can it be shown again, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Please, Witness, in this document you describe precisely the situation that you talked about just now. I don't want to dwell on it very long. You said that some commanders in units and some entire units became disobedient, and you were informed about that, and then you talk about the lack of command staff, and then also you say that there is logistic security that is poor. You've already told us all of that. The Prosecutor showed us, a few minutes ago, a document that talks -- well, it's page 2 of this document, rather, Your Honours, so could we see that again, page 2? Page 2. Actually, the Prosecutor indicated to you here, at the very end of this page: "A special security problem in our area of responsibility," you said, and I quote: " ... Are members of other units who are out of control of their superior commands, and primarily these are members of the 7th Muslim Brigade, and the status of the Mujahedin is something that we are not fully aware of." And then arbitrary behaviour is referred to. Witness, please, is it not clear that this document fully separates the 7th Muslim Brigade from the status of the Mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Please, you -- in the field, did you ever experience the following: That members of the 7th Muslim Brigade were the same as the Muslims in Mehuric? Do you understand my question?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Have you finished that question?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Members of the 7th Muslim Brigade were never stationed in Mehuric, as far as I know, and there was personnel that was on furlough.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'll ask you about that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'll have to interrupt a little bit. I'm sorry, when you started quoting from the document, we were still on the previous page in the English. I'm trying to -- we've now been turned over to the next page. I'm trying to find the quotation, Madam Vidovic, from this document. If you can please direct us, on the English page, where you quoted from. Your quotation, I think, started where: "Are members of other units who are out of control of their superior commands ..."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 2, English version. Can you please -- Your Honours, the last section.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like you to look at the continuation on page 3. That's what I was talking about to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document can be removed now, and I would like us to show the witness MFI 255, 255, MFI 255, page 2. Your Honours, I'm sorry, it's page 3, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, could you please carefully read this part: "In the area of responsibility, serious problem --" Your Honours, it says here: "In the 3rd Corps area of responsibility ..." That's where it starts. Witness, I'm going to quote this to you now: "In the 3rd Corps area of responsibility, arbitrary activity of certain parts and members of the 7th Muslim Brigade and the 314th Motorised Brigade which got out of control of their commands represents a significant security problem. As a consequence of this, the already tense situation with the HVO units is becoming more complex. "On the 24th of April, 1993, members of the 7th Muslim Brigade attacked the village of Gornji Miletici inhabited by Croat population on which occasion five villagers were killed." Please, Witness, a few moments ago I showed you the report of the 306th Brigade. You agreed that this report refers on one page to the problems with the 7th Brigade and in another place problems with the Mujahedin; am I right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Please, did you ever report that members of the 7th Muslim attacked Miletici?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Actually, it is not correct at all that members of the 7th Muslim attacked Miletici; right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Now, please, Witness, you worked on security matters and you wrote reports and you communicated with superior commands. It is correct, is it not, that these reports are written in the following way: First, the brigade writes its report to the corps, and then the corps deals with it and submits it to a higher command; am I right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you agree that in all this writing, there can be lack of understanding and interpretations that actually never existed in the original document?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And do you agree that the original document, the initial document shown to you by the Prosecutor, has a completely different content from that which appears here about the very same event?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honours, I'll go back to some other questions related to the 7th Muslim unit later, but now this document can be removed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The document may be removed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Based on the documents that we've seen before, it can be seen that communications of the 306th Brigade were poor, communications with the outside world?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yesterday, you mentioned telegrams; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Based on that, I conclude that at the time of April, May, June 1993, the packet communications were not functioning; am I right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: It's right that until the 10th of May, 1993, the 306th Brigade did not have the packet communications; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And shortly after the packet communications arrived at the 306th, it broke down and it had to be taken for repair; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you please tell the Trial Chamber what happened with the packet communications then?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: When the unit, repair unit, was coming to fix it at the crossing in Travnik, the apparatus was confiscated, and I don't know how long they kept it. After a while, a long while, they returned it to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So because of that, in the documentation we can see telegrams?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like the witness to look at Exhibit 257, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I am going to ask you again something about the 7th Muslim Brigade. The 7th Muslim Brigade, in the Biljani region area, did not have a single unit there in early 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please look at page 2 of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, please, what is correct is that it had 50 -- approximately 50 members, which we see here, in different villages of the Bila region, and we can see Kljaci, Maline, Visnjevo, Zolote, Radojcici and so on and so forth?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Am I correct when I say that these are people who, before the blockade in mid-April 1993, came for a holiday, came to their homes, and there they were blockaded?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: They could not go back to their unit because the roads were blocked; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And because of that, the document is titled "List of Members from the 7th who are From the Bila Region," meaning who are originally from the Bila region, because all these villages are from the Bila region; correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we can put this document away, and I would now like the witness to look at D225. This is a document of the 306th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you recognise Mr. Sipic's signature, if you can?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: It's a bit hard, as far as signatures are concerned. It's been a long time since then, but it probably is.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: All right. I'm going to ask you something about this fact that is mentioned here. It's a short document. It states: "I order a part of the troops currently stationed in the Kljaci village, who are members of the 7th Muslim Brigade, shall be attached to the unit of Kljaci village." And if you could help us in relation to this, please. Is it correct that these are the people from the 7th Muslim who happened to be blocked in the village of Kljaci?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes. And if I can just comment, you can see in this document that the 306th was not functioning as an establishment unit in this period because it was being added on to the unit in the Kljaci village.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. You are trying to say that these are still village units?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like to ask you this: You can see that the commander ordered that these people who remained in the Kljaci village be reattached?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Well, he wanted to use the weapons, actually, because at the time the 306th didn't have any weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, thank you very much. Your Honours, can this document please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: This document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 268.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness please look at Exhibit 134. Exhibit 134.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, do you agree that this document talks about the lines of defence of the 306th Brigade? I would just ask you to look at the axis line of defence under number 5, Simulje, Probijeno Brdo, Ostrilo, and at the end of the document it is stated the 1st mountain Battalion, the size of one mountain company, and reinforced by the 7th Brigade platoon. When we're talking about these units, are these the same people from the list about whom you said that they happened to be at their homes at that time?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Please, I would like to draw your attention just to remember the Simulje, Probijeno Brdo, Ostrilo, because in a minute after this I'm going to ask you something in connection with another document. Your Honours, can this document be given an exhibit number? Oh, actually, it's already an exhibit. I apologise. Could the witness now look at another exhibit, Exhibit 90, unless Your Honours have questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could I just ask my learned colleague to state the exhibit number of this last exhibit for the record, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's Exhibit 134.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, 134.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So you did pay attention to this axis. Now we're looking at document 90. Your Honours, I'm not going to take too long with this document. Witness, please, can you look at this official note on the death of Sakib Brkic, and the date is the 28th of June. I think you signed this document?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is it the 28th of June or the 28th of May?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours, it's May. I made a mistake. It's the 28th of May, 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So you wrote this document, and I conclude that you are well familiar with this event. And I would just like to draw your attention to this part which contains the date, the 25th of May, 1993. It's in the middle of the document, it states: "On the 25th of May, 1993, a group of Mujahedin who are not under the control of our brigade and are billeted in Mehuric, in the area of responsibility of our brigade, without asking for permission and without having informed anyone, reconnoitered the Probijeno Brdo sector (elevation 1009)." Witness, you had information about this event. It's correct, isn't it, that the Mujahedin did not ask permission from you to reconnoiter your terrain?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes, they did not ask it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And they didn't inform you about that, either, did they?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: No, they did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: In the previous document I asked you to look at, the line of Defence, Simulje, Probijeno Brdo, Ostrilo, do you agree with me that this event actually happened specifically in that area, the Probijeno Brdo area, elevation K1009?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And I would like to ask you, who is Akif Brkic? Who is Sakib Brkic, son of Akif; did you know him well?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: I'm going to be very clear here, this is the son of my aunt. He was underaged.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Was he a member of your brigade or not?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: He was under age. Our brigade did not accept youths under-aged. He was with Ramo Durmis, in his unit, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So he had joined the Mujahedin; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this document please be put away now. And, Your Honours, a break. I apologise, I apologise. I didn't notice that it was already past that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The document may be removed, and we'll have a break and come back at quarter to 6.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, we were talking about the 7th Muslim when we stopped, and I would like to go back to your brigade now. Did a single member of your -- was a single member of your unit an Arab?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Or a Turk, a foreigner?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honours, could the witness now look at document D232.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, can you please look at the document? It's a document of the Command of the 3rd Corps of the 28th of August, 1993, order for the re-subordination of units, and the order states that - this is in paragraph 1: "A unit of the independent detachment, El Mujahedin, and its entire personnel and materiel and equipment, shall be re-subordinated to the 306th Mountain Brigade in order to perform planned combat actions." It says: "The Commander of the 306th and the Commander of the El Mujahed Unit are responsible for jointly preparing the combat actions." And can you please look at this remark written by hand: "Not implemented"?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And it's signed by Enver Hadzihasanovic. You can see that the re-subordination of El Mujahedin to your unit was ordered. Did this ever actually happen?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you have information if you ever --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Excuse me for interrupting, but do we know why it was not implemented? Does the witness know?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was precisely my next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, do you know why this was not implemented?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Very well. Did you ever, since you were not a member of the Command on the 28th of August, 1993, so did your Command, together with the El Mujahed Command, ever set out for jointly planning and preparing combat actions?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, they never did, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honours, can this document be given an exhibit number, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a question. Witness, it is said here that the El Mujahedin Detachment must be re-subordinated, if I understand properly, re-subordinated to the 306th Brigade. Does this mean that it had been subordinated to it before and then the 306th Brigade lost control of the said detachment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The El Mujahed Detachment was never re-subordinated to the 306th, and the 306th unit never had any control over it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand that it was not re-subordinated, but I wonder, before that was it ever subordinated to it? Is that the reason why there is a mention here made of re-subordination, that it could be put again under the control of the brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I know, it was never re-subordinated to the 306th. It's possible that we sometimes jointly acted in combat actions after the 8th of June, but the El Mujahed Unit was never under the command of the 306th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sir, that is understood. The question is not whether it was ever re-subordinated. The question is: Was it ever subordinated? You see, the word "re" in front of the word "subordinate" means "again," so was it ever subordinated in the first place? That's the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You are absolutely certain of that, or do you not know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, I am certain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this has nothing to do with the witness, but this question is something that I put earlier as a question of interpretation. So is the real word -- in our language, the word "pret pojinjave" [phoen], I'm not sure if that -- the correct translation is "re-subordination" in English, and perhaps this is something that we would need to consult experts on. I'm not sure that the two words mean the same thing. We don't have the word "subordinate," "Pojinjave." In our language, we only have the word "re-subordinate," "pret pojinjave" in our language in the military sense.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That may be so, but unfortunately we now go by the English language which is the official language here. And we can only interpret it, and we'll have to get interpreters to help us. But thank you so much. We've asked the question, and we've got the answer. May the document please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit number 269.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may proceed, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, testifying about the Mujahedin, you said that until the spring of 1993, they were busy with humanitarian work. Would you agree that in that way, they received a lot of support among the people?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: They also secured the support of certain imams; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Other imams, Muslim priests, rejected them because of the Vahabi stream or direction that they spread; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And that is why --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not understand Ms. Vidovic's question. Can she repeat it, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, you are being asked to repeat your question because the interpreter didn't hear you. You said "... and that is why," and you didn't finish.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And that is why there was tension in certain Muslim villages, divisions and tensions in certain Muslim villages; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: In your testimony, you said -- or rather, excuse me. You recall giving a statement to the Prosecutor on the 29th of July, 2007?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: In paragraph 44 of the statement, you said with them, speaking about the Mujahedin, you could not enter into a conflict with them because that would constitute a third front?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You already had two fronts, one in relation to the Serbian forces and the other one in relation to the Croatian Defence Council?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You would agree, then, that the third front would not only be just with the Mujahedin but with their numerous supporters in that region, primarily the local imams and their followers; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And that would then be a very difficult situation for the Muslims, would it not, fighting against two external enemies and one internal enemy in Central Bosnia; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You, in the 306th Brigade, were aware of that, were you not?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And the 3rd Corps was aware of that; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The group in Mehuric was not the only group of Mujahedin in that area; am I not right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: During 1993, Abu Hamza operated there, and you knew that he was out of the control of the group in Mehurici; am I right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: He operated around Guca Gora?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You testified that while you were on the Territorial Defence Staff, the Mujahedin shared the same building with that staff; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Please, please, do you agree that after the 306th Brigade was established and after it got into that building, the Mujahedin left the building immediately?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes, the Mujahedin, and I think that the 1st Battalion was there, the 306th. They were not in the same building, but the Mujahedin just kept one room upstairs on the second floor, if I remember well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Did they stay there or did they keep some things there?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: They just kept some of their things there. They moved to Savici Kuce.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Please, the Territorial Defence Staff did not secure these premises for the Mujahedin, did not make them available to them. You were involved in security work yourself, were you not?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes, and we did not do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, can the witness now look at Document -- Exhibit 136 shown to him by the Prosecutor. That's the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I would just like to remind you of this. On the 13th of May, 1993, you wrote that Ramo Durmis and Sljivo Malik are with the Mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Am I right if I say that they were then members of the local Mujahedin, not the 7th Muslim Brigade in any way on this day, the 13th of May, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. And now, please, I would just like you to have a look -- I think it's the very end of this document. Yes, it's the end of the document, the last section. It says here -- just wait for a moment for the English version -- in the English language, please. This section is on the previous page, and it ends here, so the Trial Chamber should be able to see this. So you said here people who have already shown themselves to be materialists, who watch out for their own interests alone, are also involved in these activities. One of them - could you please continue - is Mr. Zihnija Aganovic, president of the Travnik district, who is dishing all this up behind the scenes." Please, may I just remind you of the following? This is a document in which you describe talks of the Mujahedin on the establishment of -- well, when they're telling you that the 8th Muslim Brigade was being established. Please, on the basis of this part of your document, you're the author of this document; right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: As for this part of the document, I conclude that you did know that behind the Mujahedin and the establishment of the 8th Muslim Brigade is the President of the War Presidency of the Travnik District, Mr. Zihnija Aganovic; did I correctly understand this part of your document?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honours, this document can be removed now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Now, you knew what the structure was. Do you agree that there were -- War Presidency was not part of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina but that it was a civilian organ?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: In response to the Prosecutor's questions, you said that you had problems in the 306th Brigade because your soldiers went to the Mujahedin unit, and you said that you fought against that. Was it possible for you to go in there and to look -- enter their camp, that is, and to look for members of your brigade, if any of them went over to them?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Nevertheless, you brought criminal charges against those who left your unit and joined the Mujahedin; am I not right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, now I would like the witness to have another look at 259, Exhibit 259, the document of the 306th Brigade, dated the 24th of July, 1993, and addressed as an answer to the District Military Prosecutor's office. You confirmed, in response to the prosecutor's question, that you signed it. That's the protest to the Prosecutor's office because of inaccuracies in view of the number of criminal reports filed. And while you testified, you explained to us that the Prosecutor's Office in this case -- well, actually, could we just have the document lifted so that the names can be seen? Thank you. Please. Well, in the English language, too, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You said to us that you protested because it was stated that you had sent one, whereas you sent eleven criminal reports. Please, it is correct, isn't it, that this is not the only such case, that actually several times it happened to you, that quite simply your criminal reports were not even recorded?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Even meetings were held in respect of that, for example, by the District Prosecutor's Office; am I right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You complained about such behaviour of the Prosecutor's Office?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Is it correct that it was only the District Prosecutor's Office that was completely disabled, they just had one prosecutor and one deputy during 1993?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Also, I want to ask you the following, please: It's correct, is it not, that sometimes quite simply criminal reports were returned to you, and what was stated was: "Write better ones, these are unprofessional"?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: It happened several times, they sought additional information.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Quite simply, they did not register these reports?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: On the basis of this protest that we lodged, it seemed to me that they did not record our criminal reports at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honours, this document can be removed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Now -- well, actually, when you made a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor, the one that I referred to a few moments ago, you said that after what happened in Miletici, that is to say, after that, you had clear instructions to follow and record the activity of the Mujahedin and to report to the Command about that; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And that is, indeed, what you did?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Now I would just like to ask you about some persons. Please, do you know Isak Aganovic?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Please, can you tell the Trial Chamber whether this is a member of your brigade and, generally speaking, what you know about him in 1993?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: I think that straightaway he went to the unit of Mujahed. I mean, well, I think he even left the detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Just tell us, what is this -- when you say "straightaway," the beginning of what?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: The end of 1992, beginning of 1993, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know Ziknad Sajdic [phoen]?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'm going to put the same question in relation to him. Was he a member of your brigade, and if so, until when?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: He left, too, among the first soldiers who went to El Mujahed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you tell us approximately when this was? Was it winter, spring -- or, rather, the spring of 1993?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Possibly April 1993, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'm going to ask you whether you can Safet Dautovic?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Was he a member of your brigade?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: From the beginning until the end, I think he was a member of our brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: A member of the 306th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: From the beginning until the end of the war, you mean?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know a person nicknamed Biban?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Who was this? Tell us.

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Hodzic Habib, nicknamed Biban, he was a member of the MUP, of the civilian police.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I am going to ask you the following, briefly: You testified about what you knew about what happened in Maline, and you said that you entrusted Hasan Zukanovic with the investigation because he was an experienced pre-war policeman. Did I understand you well?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You said that he took statements from eyewitnesses; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: As for the Command of the 3rd Corps, you informed them straightaway, you personally, that there are some indications concerning the execution of about 20 persons?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You sent a telegram about that?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, D138 is my reference here. Rather, Exhibit 138. Because the witness accepts this, let us not waste time over this, unless the Honourable Trial Chamber wants to see this document. Exhibit 138. It's not indispensable. That is what I am referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Except that it was marked for identification, Madam. Maybe you could just show it to him, then we can tender it in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, all right, yes. MFI 138. I do apologise. 138. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, please look at this document. Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes. I drafted this about the execution of 20 civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you agree that at the end of the document, it says investigation is pending and upon the completion of the investigation you will be informed on time?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What is this Gabela, what does is it, "Gabela 802," mean?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: I really cannot remember now, I cannot remember. I've been thinking about it all the time. Its been a long time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: All right. Do you agree that you informed the 3rd Corps, through this telegram, about the investigation that you were carrying out?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could this document now please be admitted into evidence? Could it please be assigned a number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence, and I believe it will now be given Exhibit number 138.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour, it will be Exhibit number 138.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like the witness to see Exhibit 228. For the transcript, this is a document of the Command of the 3rd Corps, dated the 20th of June, 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You're left with nine minutes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will do my best, Your Honours, to the best of my ability.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, please look at the second sentence straightaway, because I have very little time. You will see that it's a document of the 3rd Corps, and you see the name of Commander Enver Hadzihasanovic?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The second sentence says: "An investigation into the events in the village of Maline has been launched, and I hope that the competent organs will be rigorous, which will be my request." I just have a question for you here. Witness, please, is it your understanding that the Commander of the 3rd Corps received information from you that an investigation was being carried out?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And that this document states this unequivocally?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: All right. Please answer the following: In the same way you said that the Mujahedin had committed this, not the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina; am I right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Now, I would just like to remind you of that document. The Prosecutor showed it to you of Mr. Osman Fusko. This was a member of your organ; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Desk officer of the Military Security Service.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: All right. I don't want us to waste any time. You remember -- you've seen it; right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Please, did you give Mr. Fusko instructions to write that document in the way in which it was written?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You said to us that you couldn't have -- or, rather, that you weren't there at all; right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Most probably, I said -- well, most probably, I was not there, but I first saw this document at the trial in 2005.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honours, in relation to this, I would like the witness to have a look at Exhibit 89, Exhibit 89, very briefly. Can we scroll the document down so that we can see?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You said that you were at the Forward Command Post. Can you please look at this part of the document? This is a document of the 306th Brigade which says in the Parica Greda region, the Command for this axis was deployed comprising officers of the brigade, operatives persons, moralist, and communications person. Is this the Forward Command Post that you were talking about?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. After the commander, Mr. Sipic, was replaced, you were very frequently at that Forward Command Post; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Was it possible for you to issue instructions from there?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: No, because of the communications. We used radio relay communications from up there. The telephone and the other system like that is something that I would never use to give information of this kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And I just have one more question on this. It's correct, isn't it, that in June, July, and August of 1993, before you left to Parica Greda, the Deputy of the 3rd Corps, Dzemal Merdan, came to the broader area of there; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: He went there with representatives of the International Community and Father Stipan Radic?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honours, I'm going to -- well, maybe this document can be put away. I just have a question for the witness in relation to Exhibit 263. And just if the witness can briefly look at the document. All right. Can the witness look at the very last excerpt from the document, the one that the Prosecutor questioned him about?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you agree that it is at Hrasce, elevation 688?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You confirm that it was elevation 688?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe we can put this document away, and maybe the document -- the witness can look at Exhibit 182. This is a document or exhibit under seal, and then if we can, in a minute, finish. This is Exhibit 172 under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you want us to move into private session?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm told it's not under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. If the witness can briefly look at this document. Your Honours, this is not the document. 172.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You asked for 182. We have given you 182. Do you want 172?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 172, please. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May we move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are now in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If, please, Exhibit 139 could be shown to this witness. It's an exhibit marked for identification, and I'm referring to page 81 of today's transcript. My learned colleague, just a few minutes ago, has mentioned a visit of (redacted)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I believe that's under seal, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Is that under seal? Sorry, then we would need to go into private session. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are now in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Who, specifically, in this 3rd Corps security section did you deal with about the Mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: We would hand that in -- in writing, the information, what we had, what we could get, but it was very difficult to find anything out from them. Right at the outset, I said that these were people who were constantly on the move, you know. You could not get their names or passports.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, please listen to the question. The question is: To who in this 3rd Corps security section did you deal with about the Mujahedin? As you report up the ladder of command, who --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My superior, the security chief, Dugalic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Was there also somebody in counter-intelligence section you were dealing with in the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: I cannot remember, but I think it was Osman Vlajicic for a while. But I didn't discuss this topic with him. We talked about other things, mostly the information I had about the Serbian-Montenegrin aggressor, relating to counter-intelligent affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: No further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do have a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: In what capacity did the 3rd Corps deal with the El Mujahedin Detachment. It's not very clear to me. Could you please shed some light on this? As far as you know, what is the capacity?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: It's not what they were interested in, the superior military security organ, names of persons that we could get, where they were going, and the entire incidents that they created for us was something that we reported on about in official notes, which we then submitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just wanted to point out something about the translation. It's a matter of translation, Your Honours. Something that the witness did not say has been recorded. He said on page 87, line 21, "That's what they were interested in." Page 87. At least that's what I have on the screen. And the question, line 21 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Line 21 is where you are speaking, Madam Vidovic. I'm not quite sure what -- okay, "It's not what they were interested in," right? That's line --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. Actually, the witness said the opposite, so I would like to clarify that with the witness. He said, "That's what they were interested in." Perhaps that needs to be clarified with the witness. Otherwise, it's very unclear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, but do you understand, Madam Vidovic, you know, I did say this to you a couple of days ago, that when the Bench is asking questions and there are mistakes, let the Bench ask questions and finish. When they're finished, you can clear the problem. I'm not sure now where we are at this stage. The Judge is in the middle of asking questions. You've risen up while the witness was talking. Can you wait until the Judge is over with with their questions, and then you can clear this point up. Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I might repeat the question. The only thing I wanted to know is some clarification. What were the questions with which your superiors in the 3rd Corps would deal with with regard to El Mujahedin Detachment? You may have said so already, but I would like to have some further clarifications in this respect.

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: I said that they wanted their personal data, who they were, what they were, where did they come from, what they were doing, what were they dealing with, their movements, where they were going, the normal things that we could monitor. What we could monitor, we would send information on, and what we couldn't, we couldn't. They were constantly moving around.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have another question. If they were not soldiers, this was not within their jurisdiction of the civilian police, how was -- how were the powers distributed in matters of security, of state security, between the civilian police and the military police?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: In the depth of the territory, the military police did not have any authority other than over members of the 306th Brigade. Our territory was where our responsibility lay, in that outside of our area of responsibility it was the civilian police who were in charge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Sorry, Madam Vidovic, can you clarify that point?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise because when the transcript is wrong, then I'm afraid that then the Trial Chamber also will be misled. The witness said, and this is page 89, lines 7 to 11, he said what -- he didn't say, "What was outside of our area of responsibility." He mentioned the territory in the depth, and that's quite different. "In the depth," it means towards the interior and not like this outside of the territory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So what should, in your view, be the correct interpretation of what the witness said? Maybe we should ask the witness again.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, that would be best, to ask the witness again, better than for me to interpret.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm asking you, Madam Vidovic, because you know what you need to have recorded. Ask him.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Witness, please, you said that the jurisdiction of the civilian police was in the depth of the territory; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: And what did you mean by that expression?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Well, the area of responsibility was on the defence line of our brigade. In the depth within, we just had jurisdiction over members of the 306th Mountain Brigade; that is to say that we had no authority over Mujahed, or the civilian population, or anyone else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Witness, this begs the question of whether you did not have jurisdiction over war crimes committed within the area of responsibility of your brigade. I would imagine that the military police would have jurisdiction over all -- [overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes, if we're talking about members of the 306th Mountain Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Whereas war crimes committed by the opposing party, the other army, or a third army, would not fall under the jurisdiction of the military police; is that what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: My brigade, the 306th, had jurisdiction over members of the 306th. If we were talking about civilians, then it was the civilian police, because a unit like El Mujahed, I told you, we had no jurisdiction over them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I understand your perception to be that, in physical terms, you couldn't enter the premises of their camp, so you had no factual possibility of going in and actually asking questions to anyone inside the Mujahedin camp in Mehurici. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: But you will also appreciate that there is a legal question here, because we have seen documents during your testimony which seem to suggest that, from a legal point of view, the El Mujahedin Detachment should be subordinated under the 3rd Corps, so I want to clarify whether your statement, that you had no jurisdiction over crimes possibly committed by the Mujahedin, whether that statement relates to the fact that you could not enter the premises of their camp and could not conduct your investigations inside the Mujahedin camp, and the factual impossibility alone.

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: We did not have any jurisdiction over them, as I said, and thereby we could not enter. I did not see at that point in time any unit, organisation, military, police, civilian, any organisation that could enter their camp in order to carry out an investigation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Right. But, Witness, please help me here. My question is whether your statement, that you had no jurisdiction, is based exclusively on the fact that you simply couldn't enter the premises.

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: We had no jurisdiction over them and we couldn't enter, either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So you are now saying that it was not only the factual impossibility of going inside the Mujahedin camp that prevented you from carrying out the investigation; it was also a legal assertion that the members of the Mujahedin Detachment were, legally speaking, outside the jurisdiction of the military police; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes, because when the crime was committed, I said already that they were not in the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina at all, and I don't think that there were any possibilities that we had or we did not have any jurisdiction over them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I understand, but who told you that you had no legal jurisdiction? I'm asking because we see -- or we have seen here during your testimony documents from that very same period of time, discussing exactly the issue of how to subordinate the Mujahedin Detachment under the legal responsibility of the 3rd Corps, so who told you that you had no legal jurisdiction?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: I consulted my desk officer, Jusic, and everything that he said to me, and other persons who were relevant in terms of telling me. Well, we did not have any jurisdiction over the members of the El Mujahed, and also other members of the army who were from other units. We would just inform their superior commands if they had caused an incident or had done something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: But yet you were the one who initiated the investigation in the first place, as I recall.

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes, but at the moment when I realised that no members of the 306th Brigade had taken part in that, my hands were tied. There was no way in which I could have entered the camp of the El Mujahed Unit and carried out investigations there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: No, I understand that very well. Even if you had tried, you would be expelled or you would not be allowed entrance, so from a physical point of view, it was impossible. Now, let me attack this same issue from another angle. If crimes possibly committed by the Mujahedin were outside, legally speaking, outside your jurisdiction, then I assume it would fall under the jurisdiction of the civilian police, would it not?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: And you would then -- or I'm asking you: Did you then or did anyone in the 306th Brigade have any contact with the civilian police in the area in order to see that an investigation was carried out?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: The civilian police was aware of this. I remember some details and conversations. I cannot confirm exactly now, but I think that they had filed some criminal reports against unknown persons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Did you have the feeling or the impression that the investigation was being stopped?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: As I've said, at the moment when we obtained this information, who the perpetrators were, we really did not have jurisdiction to investigate any further. We informed the superior command, and as far as we were concerned that was the end of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I don't quite remember, but when you went to the camp, the Mujahedin camp, and when you could not enter the camp, I do remember correctly, don't I? And when did you go to the Mujahedin camp, why did you go to the Mujahedin camp, and why did you try to enter the camp if you had no responsibility over whatever they did?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: I was asked by the commander for us to go together and to talk to them so that if things like the kind of things that happened -- happening, would not happen again. But I've already said we were up against a rock. They wouldn't even let us go in. And I told you the rest of the story.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sir, am I right to say that according to you, these people who were killed in Maline were kidnapped from the soldiers of the Army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina by foreigners?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So these were people who were found in Maline, and they were in a group of 300 people who had been taken to Mehurici for their own protection?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Therefore, the Army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina had the responsibility to look after the safety and security of these people, all of them, up until they get to their safe place in Mehurici?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes, but there weren't enough people. Combat operations were going on. As far as I can remember, five military policemen were escorting that column.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sir, I hear that. I'm asking you about the legal responsibility of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. They had the legal responsibility to look for -- to secure the safety up until they get to the place of safety in Mehurici?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: The army did its best to secure the safety of their trip, but what happened happened and they were attacked, these people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes. Will you please listen to my questions. I'm not asking you of what the army did, physically. I'm asking you of the legal responsibility of the army, and I repeat myself. The army that was taking these people to Mehurici had the legal responsibility to ensure their safety and security until they got to a safe place in Mehurici; am I right.

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: You are right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, if --

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- if anybody then takes these people from the army, that does not relieve the army of their legal responsibility to see to the security of these people; is that correct? That duty doesn't fall away simply because the army isn't capable physically to do the job?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes, but the army was doing its best to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Therefore, therefore, when somebody has taken these people and commits crime upon these people, the army is still legally obliged to pursue that person, whoever it is?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm not a lawyer by training. I'm saying --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm just asking you. If somebody takes from you your property, sir, you have the right to pursue this person until you get your property back, and if he refuses, you have the right to prosecute this person.

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes, but again I repeat that, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, thank you. If I need an explanation, I'll ask you to explain. Now, in this instance, these people who actually kidnapped these civilians or these prisoners of war, or whatever they are, had actually been fighting side by side with the army, am I right, the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: In that period, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm talking of on that day in particular.

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, they were not fighting us. They ran out of the forest and abducted these people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If they were not fighting you, who were they fighting?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: They were not fighting us, but they were not acting in concert with --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You've told us that. My question is simple. Who were they fighting?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Well, that day our army that was working on the deblockade of Velika Bukovica did not plan on the El Mujahed Unit, did not cooperate with it, as far as I know, as far as I have been informed, but they were nearby. They were near that battlefield, and they could hear what was going on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Delalic, is my question so difficult? My question is very simple. Who were they fighting?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Well, you're putting me in an embarrassing situation. I'm trying to explain that they did not cooperate, they did not act in concert with us. Those who fight with us, who act in concert with us, do not abduct people from us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now my question -- what is so embarrassing about my question? I'm asking a very simple question. Who were these people who kidnapped these people fighting? Who were they fighting? What's so embarrassing about that question?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: The question is unclear to me for the following reason: They did not act in concert with us at that moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's not the question I'm asking you, sir. I'm asking you a very simple -- don't complicate my question. My question is: Who were they fighting against? Don't make it any more complicated than it is.

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm not complicating things. They were fighting against the Serb-Montenegrin aggressor and the HVO, but they were not acting in concert with us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now, if they are not acting in concert with you, you then have the duty, as the Bosnian Army, to protect those in your custody against them, don't you?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: We did protect them, as far as I know, and if we didn't manage to protect them, then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And to the extent that you failed to protect these, you bear the legal responsibility, don't you?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: From what I said, and I think I said at the beginning, that I was at the Forward Command Post in Rudnik under a blockade for 20 days, and I couldn't influence the unit that was going to take these people --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm not asking you that, sir. My questions have always been directed against the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. I'm saying to the extent that people kidnapped captives from the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, to that extent the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina bears the legal responsibility to make sure that those people are safe, and if they are not, to pursue the abductors.

utterances.speaker: ASIM DELALIC
utterances.text: I entirely agree with you, Your Honours, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. That ends my questions. We will resume tomorrow at 9.00 in the morning in Courtroom II. You will come back to court at 9.00 tomorrow morning in Courtroom II, sir. Okay? Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 28th day of August, 2007, at 9.00 a.m.
